# scaling_working_hours (Resource)

Manages a named, reusable Working Hours set — a timezone plus weekly windows — used by escalation policy step conditions for follow-the-sun routing.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A Working Hours set is a named, reusable timezone + weekly windows. The
# timezone lives on the set and is never inferred from a targeted schedule.
# Escalation policy step conditions reference a set to drive follow-the-sun
# routing ("page the UK rotation during UK hours, the US rotation otherwise").
resource "scaling_working_hours" "uk_office" {
  name     = "UK office hours"
  timezone = "Europe/London"

  window {
    days  = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5] # Monday–Friday (ISO weekday numbers, 1=Mon)
    start = "09:00"
    end   = "17:00"
  }
}

resource "scaling_working_hours" "us_office" {
  name     = "US office hours"
  timezone = "America/New_York"

  window {
    days  = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
    start = "08:00"
    end   = "18:00"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Display name of the working hours set. Unique within your organization.
- `timezone` (String) IANA timezone the windows are interpreted in (e.g. "Europe/London"). The timezone lives on the set; it is never inferred from a targeted schedule.

### Optional

- `window` (Block List) Weekly windows during which these hours are active. At least one window is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--window))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) ISO 8601 creation timestamp.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the working hours set.
- `org_id` (String) Organization that owns this working hours set.
- `updated_at` (String) ISO 8601 last-update timestamp.

<a id="nestedblock--window"></a>
### Nested Schema for `window`

Required:

- `days` (List of Number) ISO weekday numbers this window applies to (1=Monday through 7=Sunday).
- `end` (String) Window end time as 24-hour HH:MM in the set's timezone.
- `start` (String) Window start time as 24-hour HH:MM in the set's timezone.
